articles.title: Man City titles 'absolutely not' tainted - Maresca
articles.summary: Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca says the club's titles are "absolutely not" tainted after they were found guilty of the majority of the 115 charges brought against them by the Premier League.
body: Maresca reiterated his faith in the club's owners and belief that they will win their appeal against the verdict during a news conference on Friday dominated by questions on the matter.
The Italian, notably relaxed as he offered his responses, rejected the suggestion City's titles have been tainted by the ruling, as he knows "exactly the effort that the club put in to achieve" them.
An independent commission found Manchester City guilty of all charges relating to breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons.
The club have appealed against the verdict and claimed in a statement the commission's ruling contained "clear material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe".

articles.title: Zavier Gozo: ‘You have to be uncomfortable to get to the highest levels’
articles.summary: Crystal Palace’s American import had never lived anywhere but Utah before moving to London. Now, he’s aiming for more Premier League minutes. Much has changed in Zavier Gozo’s life since May.
body: Back then, Gozo was a day removed from learning that he wasn’t among Mauricio Pochettino’s 26 selections for the World Cup, having just made what proved to be his third-to-last appearance with boyhood club Real Salt Lake.
Gozo had only ever lived in Utah at that point. He would watch the World Cup from home, where he lived with his mother.
Today, less than five months later, he lives half a world away, is getting Premier League minutes and, as of a week ago, his first cap with the senior US men’s national team.

“It’s a big change to go from Utah to London,” said this master of understatement, stationed on a sofa in the lobby of the team’s downtown Minneapolis hotel in shorts, slippers, and a pristine white hoodie.

articles.title: European FAs pushing for three-week international break to be abandoned
articles.summary: Workload, injuries and finances underpin concerns. Most European FAs want return to previous format. Europe’s football associations have raised serious concerns about the impact of the extended international break and will ask Uefa to push for a reversion to the previous scheduling.
body: The new three-week break left European countries tasked with four Nations League games, which typically took place within 11 days. It has brought deep misgivings about player workload, injuries and financial viability, with one FA president telling the Guardian it was “a disaster” and numerous others saying the schedule is unworkable.

Opposition to the break was virtually unanimous when it was discussed at a meeting of European FAs in Berlin on Thursday, the subject understood to have prompted a series of passionate interventions. The Football Association chair, Debbie Hewitt, and chief executive, Mark Bullingham, were among those to speak out highlighting the drawbacks of a calendar change approved by the Fifa council in 2023. Many expressed clear preference for the set of five two-week breaks that preceded this season.

articles.summary: In-form Sale full-back Joe Carpenter admits part of him is focused on outshining Harlequins' George Furbank this weekend to advance his case for an England recall.
body: Only Exeter wing Immanuel Feyi-Waboso has beaten more defenders in the first two rounds of the Prem this season, as Carpenter has shown a keen attacking edge.

Furbank was England's first-choice full-back this summer before an appendicitis sidelined him for last summer's Nations Championship, while Carpenter has not been involved in Steve Borthwick's set-up since winning his only Test cap in a 40-5 win over the United States in July 2025.
Their two sides meet at Sale's Corpacq Stadium on Sunday, with Quins looking for their first points of a miserable campaign so far.
"Yeah I'd say so, in a certain aspect," said Carpenter when asked if the personal duel with Furbank was motivation.

articles.title: Dolphins CB Chris Johnson splits snaps like star Devon Witherspoon
articles.summary: Dolphins rookie CB Chris Johnson splits snaps between outside and nickel corner, a rare versatility that mirrors Seahawks star Devon Witherspoon
body: MIAMI GARDENS ― The topic of conversation was outside cornerback versus nickel cornerback and whether the latter can be considered a premium position in the NFL in 2026.

"Witherspoon," Miami Dolphins rookie corner Chris Johnson said, referring to Seahawks star corner Devon Witherspoon. "He plays both and he goes back and forth and he's the second highest-paid corner in the league."
For anyone who has said of Chris Johnson: "How could the Dolphins use a first-round draft pick on a cornerback and then play him at nickel?" we present the case of Witherspoon and Johnson.
The Dolphins (0-4) host the Bengals (2-2) on Sunday Oct. 11 at Hard Rock Stadium (1 p.m., Fox) and most attention this season, deservedly so, has been on Miami's rookies.

articles.title: ECB help would make women's Test a 'certainty' - West Indies
articles.summary: West Indies are still hopeful of hosting England in a women's Test next year, but the fixture would be a "certainty" if the ECB were to help fund it, says chief executive Chris Dehring.
body: ECB chair Richard Thompson suggested on Monday the board could step in to help the hosts, who have recently revealed significant financial pressures, to maintain the red-ball element of the multi-format tour.
England, in part at least, want the Test to go ahead to aid their preparations for next summer's Ashes while it will be a first women's Test for West Indies since 2004.
"We would welcome any assistance of our much wealthier member boards," Dehring told BBC Sport.

Cricket tours often involve reciprocal arrangements between boards over costs. They usually mean the home board pick up the logistical expenses of the visitors, including things like travel and accommodation.

He's having a breakout year and is a big reason why the Raiders are arguably the surprise team of the Austin area with a gaudy 6-0 record heading into Friday's District 25-6A showdown at Lake Travis.

His 73 tackles and 4½ sacks not only catch the attention of media and opposing coaches, but also college scouts. And having just turned 17 over the summer, the 6-foot-2, 213-pound senior is just scratching the surface of his physical talent.

articles.title: Kompany remains ‘proud’ of City achievements during 11 years at club
articles.summary: Former Manchester City captain Vincent Kompany said he remains “proud” of his achievements with the club despite them being found guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules.
body: Kompany spent more than a decade with City between 2008 and 2019, lifting the Premier League trophy four times, also winning the FA Cup twice and the League Cup four times.
An independent commission has found that City broke financial rules across nine seasons from 2009-10 to 2017-18, a period which covers three of the Premier League titles Kompany won with City.

The Bayern Munich head coach said: “I played 11 years for the club. I’ve loved all of the years I played for the club and everything we achieved and done on the pitch, that’s something I’m really proud of.

“Everything else, as a player you’re not a part of that and right now as a coach of Bayern Munich I’m not too much occupied with that topic as I’m preparing the game next week and preparing the game we have tomorrow and everything I have as a coach.”
